title: 2real framework config
description: The single shared-config object every genericised framework artifact (hooks, libs, skills) reads. Installed at <repo>/.claude/framework.config.json by the bootstrapper. Nearly all fields are optional and fall back to the defaults documented here, so a minimal config is just {"version":1,"scm":{"provider":"github","owner":"my-org"}}.

version.description: Config schema version. Bumped only on a breaking change to this schema.

project.description: Human-facing identity of the project this config governs.

model.description: single-repo: one repository. meta-and-children: a parent meta-repo that .gitignores N child repos (the cross-repo orchestration model).

meta_repo.description: Name of the meta-repo (meta-and-children model only). The repo that holds the shared .claude/ config.

repos.description: Repos in scope (meta-and-children model). Bare names, resolved under scm.owner. Single-repo projects omit this.

scm.description: Source-control + host provider settings. Read by every git/gh-aware hook and lib.

provider.description: Only github is implemented today; the field exists so a future provider (gitlab, …) is a config change, not a code fork.

owner.description: GitHub org or user that owns the repo(s). Used to qualify bare repo names and gh calls.

allow_force.description: When false, force-push / force-merge guards are active.

branch.description: Branch-name grammar. Tokens in braces are substituted by the skills/hooks that mint or validate branches.

integration.description: Wave/iteration integration branch (meta-and-children / wave model). Tokens: {phase} {wave}.

board.description: Planning-board (GitHub Projects v2) settings. Omit the whole block if the project does not use a board.

project_number.description: GitHub Projects v2 number under scm.owner.

wave_field.description: Single-select field name the wave label projects onto.

identity.description: Commit-identity convention. Read by the commit-identity hooks and the trust/roster libs.

enforce.description: When true, per-commit identity is validated against the roster + email pattern.

roster_source.description: Path (repo-relative) to the roster manifest the identity hooks read.

allow_emails.description: Bare author emails accepted without matching the persona pattern (e.g. the owner).

policy.description: Process policy knobs read by the PR / merge / review gates.

reviewers_required.description: Approving reviewers required before merge (the N-reviewer gate).

merge_model.description: Per-iteration merge model. wave-branch: PRs base on the integration branch, integration PR at wrapup. direct-to-main: PRs base on the default branch.

admin_merge_exceptions.description: Map of <class> -> <human rationale> naming the only admin-merge bypass classes the CI gate accepts via ADMIN_MERGE_EXCEPTION=<class>:<rationale>. Empty = no admin bypass allowed.

merge_requires_green.description: Block gh pr merge when the PR's statusCheckRollup is failing/pending.

empty_rollup_is_blocking.description: Treat an empty statusCheckRollup as not-ready (subject to the covering-workflow discriminator). 'No checks reported' is not the same as green.

neutral_pending_check_prefixes.description: CheckRun display-name prefixes whose NEUTRAL conclusion means 'review pending' (treated as pending), not 'no opinion' (treated as pass). E.g. ['chromatic'].

tooling.description: The complete CI check-set (linters/formatters/type/test/spell/…) the local<->CI parity gate expects mirrored in pre-commit. E.g. ['ruff','mypy','pytest'].

shell.description: The dev/agent shell. When 'zsh', the zsh-wordsplit safety warner is meaningful (bash-isms that silently break under zsh).

paths.description: Repo-relative locations of framework artifacts. Defaults match the bootstrap install layout.

team.description: Charter + roster + trust matrix + feedback log.

state_file.description: The wave/iteration state file the lifecycle skills read/write.

events_log.description: Where hooks append block/event records (the generic observability stream).

hooks.description: The dispatcher seam: which hook modules are active and in what order. The bootstrapper writes this; editing it enables/disables checks without touching code. Names are module names under .claude/hooks/ (no .py).

pre_bash.description: Ordered PreToolUse/Bash checks. Cheap/local first, network-calling (gh) last. First block wins.

post_bash.description: Ordered PostToolUse/Bash checks. Advisory only — never block.

post_file.description: Ordered PostToolUse checks for file-mutating tools (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit). Advisory only — never block.

session_start.description: Ordered SessionStart checks (run via start_dispatcher.py). Advisory only — never block; INERT unless the subsystem they target exists (e.g. ontology_refresh acts only when an ontology dir is present).
